meta.title: My Autumn Book — Set 4
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Sentence practice and fill-in-the-blank quiz for 'My Autumn Book'.

questions.question: What kind of wind is blowing when the narrator zips their jacket?
questions.explanation: The story says: 'A chilly wind blows. I zip my jacket.' Chilly wind is cold.

questions.question: The chipmunk scampers past with seeds packed in its mouth.
questions.explanation: False. The poem says the chipmunk has 'seeds packed in its cheeks,' not its mouth.

questions.question: In a corner of the garden shed, Spider spins a _______ thread.
questions.explanation: The story says: 'Spider spins a silken thread' in the garden shed.

questions.question: Geese honk above and fly south in formation.
questions.explanation: True. The poem states: 'Geese honk above, Fly south in formation' to escape the cold.

questions.question: Who agrees that summer is leaving with a 'rap-a-tap' drumming sound?
questions.explanation: The story says: 'Summer is leaving! Autumn coming! Woodpecker agrees, rap-a-tap drumming.'

questions.question: The cicada warns us that summer is _______.
questions.explanation: The poem states: 'Cicada is warning us: Better beware! Summer is leaving!'

questions.question: What blankets the ground in a whirlwind of color?
questions.explanation: In autumn, a whirlwind of spinning leaves blankets the ground in beautiful colors.

questions.question: Sort these tree leaf actions/colors based on their description in the story:

categories.label: Red or Brown Trees (Dogwood, Oak, Maple)

questions.explanation: Dogwood (crimson gown), oak (rust brown suit), and maple (wears red) are red/brown. Ash (cloaked in yellow) and aspen (crown of gold) are yellow/gold.

questions.question: The squirrel digs a hole to bury its treasure because it expects a change in the weather.
questions.explanation: True. The squirrel expects cold weather, so it buries food to eat during the winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe the autumn air:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The air is very crisp.' This describes the cool, fresh weather.

questions.question: What does the caterpillar know it is time to do?
questions.explanation: The poem says: 'Caterpillar knows it's time to cocoon' as autumn approaches.

questions.question: The narrator dashes to their room to decorate _______ in their book.
questions.hint: The sheets of paper in a book.
questions.explanation: The story ends with: 'I decorate pages, Arrange to make space...'

questions.question: Arrange the words to show how fast we must act:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'We have no time to delay.' The seasons change quickly, so they must act fast.

questions.question: In autumn, leaves whisper and sway in the breeze, shaking loose acorns.
questions.explanation: True. The poem states: 'Together they whisper and sway in the breeze, Shaking loose acorns and batches of leaves.'

questions.question: When crickets no longer sing and the outside world turns cold, which season has arrived?
questions.explanation: When crickets stop singing and the world turns cold and white, it is the transition into winter.
